Former Synagogue in Leutershausen

Former Synagogue · Leutershausen, Germany

The synagogue in Leutershausen (district of Ansbach) was inaugurated in 1755 in the Untere Marktgasse, replacing an earlier prayer house used by the Jewish community from around 1720. The modest three-story building, styled after the nearby Ansbach synagogue, included a women's gallery and a small ritual bath in its basement. Following the expulsion of the Jewish community in October 1938, the town acquired the building along with other Jewish-owned property. It later served as a stable for billeted troops and postwar as housing, before a private owner purchased and renovated it in 1955. Only the outer walls are believed to retain original fabric; the building today is used as a private residence.
